questions.prompt: **Exergy** of a system is best described as…
choices: The maximum useful work obtainable as it reaches the dead state
questions.explanation: Exergy is the maximum useful work available as a system reversibly equilibrates with the environment — a quality measure, not total energy.

questions.prompt: A large lake of lukewarm water at the environment temperature has…
choices: Large internal energy but essentially zero exergy
questions.explanation: At the dead state ($T = T_0$) there is no temperature difference to exploit, so the work potential (exergy) is ~zero despite huge internal energy.

questions.prompt: Unlike energy, exergy in a real process is…
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved; exergy is destroyed by irreversibilities ($X_{dest} = T_0 S_{gen} > 0$).

questions.prompt: Which heat source has the **highest** exergy per kJ, with $T_0 = 300$ K?
questions.explanation: Exergy fraction is $1 - T_0/T$, which grows with $T$. At 900 K it is $1 - 300/900 = 0.67$, the highest here.

questions.prompt: To locate where a power plant wastes the most work potential, you should compute…
choices: The exergy destruction ($T_0 S_{gen}$) in each component
questions.explanation: Component-by-component exergy destruction pinpoints the biggest irreversibilities — something a first-law (energy) balance can't reveal.

questions.prompt: A 40%-efficient power plant has a second-law efficiency of about 70%. This means…
choices: It captures 70% of the exergy actually available for its task
questions.explanation: Second-law efficiency compares output to the reversible ideal for the same source/sink, so it is higher than the thermal efficiency — only 70% of the *available* work is captured.

questions.prompt: The exergy of heat $Q$ from a reservoir at $T$ (environment $T_0$) is…
questions.explanation: The Carnot factor $(1 - T_0/T)$ weights the heat by its convertibility to work.

questions.prompt: The exergy destroyed in a process is…
questions.explanation: Gouy–Stodola: destroyed exergy is entropy generation valued at the dead-state temperature.

questions.prompt: The flow exergy of a stream (neglecting KE/PE) is…
questions.explanation: Flow exergy subtracts the unavailable part $T_0(s - s_0)$ from the enthalpy difference relative to the dead state.

questions.prompt: Heat $Q = 800$ kJ is supplied from a source at **500 K** with $T_0 = 300$ K. Find its exergy, in kJ.
A device generates entropy at $\dot S_{gen} = 0.5$ kW/K with $T_0 = 290$ K. Find the rate of exergy destruction, in kW.
A turbine produces 820 kJ/kg of useful work; the reversible work for the same inlet/exit is 1000 kJ/kg. Find the second-law efficiency (decimal fraction).
